newsitem.title: USA: Tyco Toys shareholders okay Mattel merger.
newsitem.headline: Tyco Toys shareholders okay Mattel merger.

text.p: Tyco Toys Inc said on Tuesday that its shareholders approved a proposed merger with Mattel Inc.
In a deal that would link the largest U.S. toy maker, Mattel, with the third largest, Tyco common shareholders will receive Mattel stock equivalent to $12.50 for each Tyco share, Tyco said.
Holders of Tyco Toys series C mandatorily convertible redeemable preferred stock will receive an equal number of an equivalent Mattel convertible redeemable preferred stock, Tyco said.
The merger is subject to regulatory approval, said Tyco, which had 1996 revenues of $721 million.

The waiting period under the Hart Scott Rodino Act will expire at the end of March 20, 1997, unless the the U.S. Federal Trade Commission movest to block the deal or extend the waiting period, Tyco said.
Mattel, which reported 1996 sales of $3.8 billion, and Tyco Toys are confident that the proposed merger does not violate antitrust laws, Tyco Toys said.
